title: SRE rotations, automation, and capacity-signal playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook codifies how Redwood SRE runs on-call rotations, maps monitoring signals to automated remediation, and gates operational actions (including deployments) to error budgets and capacity signals. It stitches together SLO-driven decisions, automated scaling, and human escalation into a single reference.

Scope: primary infra, runtime serving clusters (hosted + dedicated), autoscaling policies, PagerDuty rotations, Prometheus/Thanos alerts, and CI/CD deployment gates. Not in scope: sales/support triage procedures and customer success routing.

Key principles
- Prioritize fast detection, then containment, then mitigation.
- Automation first for repeatable noisy failures; humans for judgment and cross-service coordination.
- Use error-budget and capacity signals to gate risky operations.
- Keep runbooks executable: every step should include exact commands or links to automation endpoints.

Key signals and thresholds
- SLOs (examples):
  - API availability (99.95%/30d, 5m rolling alerts)
  - 95th p99 latency for text/generation endpoints: 200ms/99th percentile target
- Error budget burn signals:
  - Burn rate > 2x baseline over 1h -> notify secondary, start mitigation checklist
  - Burn rate > 5x over 30m -> page primary and consider deployment freeze
- Capacity signals (cluster-level):
  - GPU utilization sustained > 85% for 15m -> scale-up alarm
  - Queue length (requests/sec pending) > 1000 sustained 5m -> scale-up alarm
  - Node pre-scheduling failure rate > 2% -> site reliability investigation

Alert to automation mapping
|| Alert name || Severity || Auto-action || Human escalation || Owner ||
| p99-latency-spike | P2 | kick off prefix-cache flush + autoscale (see "automation endpoints") | If persists > 10m, page primary | serving-runtime |
| cluster-gpu-saturated | P1 | trigger horizontal node add (k8s cluster-autoscaler API) | If new nodes fail to join, page infra |
| errorbudget-fastburn | P1 | disable non-critical feature flags via FF-service API | page SRE primary + product oncall |
| queue-backpressure | P2 | sink traffic to fallback region (traffic-router API) | page primary if fallback not effective |

On-call rotation policy
- Roles: primary (first responder), secondary (backup), rotation owner (manages schedule), incident commander (IC) is appointed per major incident.
- Length: 1-week rotation for primary/secondary. Stagger rotations across teams so cross-team coverage is available.
- Handoffs: create a short status note in the team Slack #sre-oncall-handoffs channel at shift start and end with: active incidents, outstanding maintenance, capacity notes.
- Overlap: 30-minute overlap window during handoff recommended for weekday transitions.

Runbook: typical page flow (triage -> automate -> escalate)
1) Page received: read alert runbook summary, assess signal vs SLO thresholds.
2) Quick triage (5 minutes): check dashboard (Serving > p99 latency, cluster utilization, error budget burn).
3) If automated remediation exists, execute (see automation endpoints). Note action and timestamp.
4) If automation fails or service still degraded after 10m, escalate to secondary and call out product owners.
5) For P1 incidents: declare incident, assign IC, record timeline in incident doc, and follow post-incident procedures.

Automation endpoints (examples)
- Prefix cache flush: POST https://ops-api.internal/v1/actions/flush-prefix-cache {
  "service": "serving-runtime", "prefix_ttl": 10
}
- Cluster scale (k8s autoscaler trigger): curl -X POST "https://k8s-autoscaler.internal/api/v1/scale" -d '{"cluster":"prod-serving-cluster","delta_nodes":4}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN'
- Feature-flag pause: POST https://ff.internal/api/v1/flags/pause {"flag":"new-batching-routes","duration_mins":60}

Sample PromQL (alert rule)
- GPU saturation: avg_over_time(nvidia_gpu_utilization_percent{cluster="prod-serving"}[15m]) > 85
- Error budget burn: (1 - (good_requests_total[30d] / total_requests_total[30d])) / (1 - SLO_target) > 5

Deployment gating and error budgets
- Policy: Major releases to serving must pass the following checks before canary -> prod promotion:
  - error_budget_burn_rate (30m) < 2x baseline
  - cluster_gpu_utilization < 70% for the canary region
  - smoke tests (latency, correctness) pass for 10 consecutive minutes
- CI/CD action: the canary pipeline reads a gated endpoint /ops/api/v1/gates/deploy-check returning JSON {"status":"ok"|"hold", "reason":"..."}. If "hold", pipeline aborts.
- Example gate curl: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $CI_TOKEN" https://ops-api.internal/v1/gates/deploy-check?env=prod | jq .

Capacity runbook (scale-up sequence)
1) Verify metric (GPU util > 85% for 15m or queue length threshold).
2) Check recent deployment activity and scheduled maintenance windows.
3) Trigger autoscaler via API: curl -X POST https://k8s-autoscaler.internal/api/v1/scale -d '{"cluster":"prod-serving","delta_nodes":4}'.
4) Monitor node join events (k get nodes) and scheduler error rates.
5) If nodes do not join within 10m, rollback scale attempt and page infra.

Escalation matrix
- P1 (service down / major capacity failure): page primary -> if no ack 2min -> page oncall leads -> 10min -> exec major incident process and page exec staff.
- P2 (degradation): page primary -> 10min -> escalate to secondary if unresolved -> 30min -> declare incident if customer impact high.

Post-incident and review standards
- After any P1 or >3hr P2, SREs must produce a 72-hour preliminary incident note and a full post-incident review (PIR) within 7 calendar days. PIR must include: timeline, root cause hypothesis, corrective actions (short/long), owners, and a verification plan.
- Evidence artifacts required: alert graphs, runbook actions executed (with timestamps), automation logs, kube events, deployment IDs, and rollouts.
- PIR review cadence: review in SRE weekly ops triage; prioritize reliability initiatives into quarterly OKRs.

Maintenance and runbook hygiene
- Runbook owner must review and confirm accuracy quarterly.
- After any automation change, runbook examples and sample commands must be updated within 48 hours.
- Add a "last_tested" timestamp to automation endpoints and runbook steps (example: last_tested: 2026-01-28).

Appendices
- Common commands:
  - Check cluster GPU utilization: kubectl top nodes --selector=role=serving --containers
  - Look up recent deployments: kubectl get deployments -n serving -o wide --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp
- Quick links:
  - Dashboards: https://grafana.internal/d/serving/production-overview
  - PagerDuty: https://redwood.pagerduty.com
  - Ops API docs: https://ops-api.internal/docs
